items.streamTitle: European flight hoaxes disrupted operations without established attribution
items.streamSummary: Dozens of November 3–5 bomb threats led to flight diversions, security checks and fighter escorts; no explosives were found, and authorities had not established coordinated or state responsibility.
items.attribution: Associated Press — original November 5 aviation-security reporting; statements from European authorities

items.streamTitle: Activation steering exposed trade-offs between target behavior and model competence
items.streamSummary: A four-model preprint found some activation interventions improved selected AI behaviors yet degraded unrelated capabilities; frozen held-out tests exposed these trade-offs, so steering is not a universal safety knob.
items.attribution: Raj — arXiv preprint (contrastive activation intervention study, November 4)

items.streamTitle: AgentTrustCI tested tool policy, grounding and sequence—not only agent answers
items.streamSummary: A November preprint's deterministic test suite classified 55 authored agent traces correctly, including planted policy and trajectory violations; production robustness and generality are untested.
items.attribution: Gupta — arXiv preprint (Java/JUnit agent-validation prototype, November 4)

items.streamTitle: Observed aggression altered later behavior and inhibitory circuits in male mice
items.streamSummary: A controlled Nature mouse study found that observing aggression and experiencing it produced overlapping proactive behavior and neural inhibition changes; circuit reactivation reversed part of the effect. Human transfer remains untested.
items.attribution: Iravedra-García et al. — Nature (mouse behavioral and neural experiment, November 4)

items.streamTitle: SocioVerse2 separated evolving simulated populations from editable research workflows
items.streamSummary: A September open-source social-simulation preprint introduced longitudinal counterfactual branching, timestamped external signals and controlled research-state versions. Case demonstrations do not validate human intervention predictions.
items.attribution: Zhang et al. — arXiv preprint (SocioVerse2 simulation framework, September 21)

items.streamTitle: C2PA 2.5 specified verifiable media provenance without claiming content truth
items.streamSummary: The C2PA Content Credentials specification defines signed provenance manifests, asset bindings and validation, but does not certify the factual truth of the media or show reduced misinformation exposure.
items.attribution: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity — Content Credentials 2.5 (official technical specification)

items.streamTitle: Adaptive network rewiring improved simulated cooperation under partner failures
items.streamSummary: In synthetic 50–200-node collaboration networks, a multi-agent RL approach reported 34.7–41.2% efficiency gains and retained 78.3% performance after 15% random node loss. These are simulated organizational outcomes.
items.attribution: Peng, Li and Li — Scientific Reports (multi-agent reinforcement-learning simulations)

items.streamTitle: Celebrity persona changes appealed differently to supporters and skeptics
items.streamSummary: In a Chinese student study, intellectual persona reformulation improved views especially among low-preference audiences; strength-oriented cues reduced preference among existing fans. ERP signals are correlational and do not uniquely identify psychological processes.
items.attribution: Zhu and Wu — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (audience and ERP study)

items.streamTitle: Complex-systems researchers called for agent-accessible simulation interfaces
items.streamSummary: A November 4 Perspective argues that executable complex-systems models need structured, discoverable controls and outputs for AI-agent research workflows. It offers design requirements, not an experimentally verified prediction improvement.
items.attribution: Cattuto and Vespignani — npj Complexity (methodological Perspective)

items.streamTitle: Preprimary education laws were associated with later gender attitudes and decision participation
items.streamSummary: Across 495 representative surveys covering almost 6.7 million women in 117 countries, eligibility for preprimary education laws was associated with later schooling, less acceptance of wife-beating and more household decision participation. Implementation and confounding remain limitations.
items.attribution: Lou et al. — Nature Human Behaviour (cross-national quasi-experimental analysis)

items.streamTitle: Pure-blue quantum-dot emitters improved high-brightness XR microdisplay prospects
items.streamSummary: New blue QLED devices retained 95% of peak efficiency at 50,000 cd/m² in one architecture and supported 560-pixel-per-inch patterning. These are component tests, not operational or user-experience evaluations.
items.attribution: Bai et al. — Nature Photonics (quantum-dot display engineering)

items.streamTitle: Narrative analysis exposed concentrated opposition concealed by aggregate sentiment
items.streamSummary: Graphika contrasted broad GLP-1 social listening with community-and-narrative analysis: overall negative stance was 25%, while the adverse-effects narrative was 94% negative. The data sources and constructs were not matched for a controlled comparison.
items.attribution: Alexandra Matheny — Graphika (vendor-authored descriptive comparison)

items.streamTitle: LLM self-descriptions conveyed personality cues while differing from human texts
items.streamSummary: Seven language models and 70 German-speaking people provided 140 self-descriptions judged by six models and ten people. Judges inferred traits and detected text origin; linguistic resemblance is not evidence of genuine or stable AI personality.
items.attribution: Koerner, Egloff and Osterholz — Scientific Reports (human and LLM text-judgment study)

items.streamTitle: Likely deepfake candidate allegations circulated through known Storm-1516 amplifiers
items.streamSummary: Graphika judged two October 20 videos very likely AI-generated and assessed that the Russia-aligned Storm-1516 network produced them, based on media and network indicators. Audience belief and electoral effects were not measured.
items.attribution: Graphika Research Team — original influence-network investigation (October 21)

items.streamTitle: Human claustrum neurons tracked uncertainty and prediction error during avoidance learning
items.streamSummary: Epilepsy-patient recordings found 31 of 110 claustrum neurons associated with model-derived uncertainty and 25 with prediction error. Claustrum and anterior-cingulate signals differed in timing; the evidence is neural correlation in a small clinical sample.
items.attribution: Hu et al. — Nature Neuroscience (single-neuron observations; research briefing November 4)

items.streamTitle: Election Day glitches and unrelated images were rapidly turned into unverified fraud narratives
items.streamSummary: AP's November 3 case checks separated a genuine New York scanner fault from unverified sabotage claims, disproved a Houston ballot-raid rumor and documented false Georgia polling texts of unknown origin.
items.attribution: Melissa Goldin and Calvin Woodward — Associated Press (original Election Day fact checks)

items.streamTitle: NATO outlined a cross-domain synchronization problem, not a measured capability gain
items.streamSummary: NATO ACT's November 3 report describes four priorities for military–civilian multi-domain coordination across 30 nations. The conference was an implementation forum, not an evaluated improvement in operational effects.
items.attribution: NATO Allied Command Transformation — November 3 official conference report

items.streamTitle: Audit-task LLM agents yielded to some professional pressure but resisted a client inducement
items.streamSummary: Across twelve LLM audit settings, professional authority cues shifted some agent judgments without new evidence, while client career inducements often reduced revision. The behavior is not validated as human conformity.
items.attribution: Richard Zhe Wang — arXiv preprint (delegated-audit agent experiment)

items.streamTitle: Eye-tracking-informed cues improved some immersive 3D network-analysis judgments
items.streamSummary: A 2026 IEEE paper used VR eye tracking to study 3D network analysis and derive visual cues that improved correctness in most follow-up trials. Real-world analytic transfer remains untested.
items.attribution: Wang et al. — IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (VR eye-tracking studies)

items.streamTitle: A 500-million-persona synthetic economy emphasized the gap between scale and behavioral validity
items.streamSummary: S²-MAS reported 500 million synthetic household personas and 12 million simulated agents, with explicit decision/state separation. Its model's 38.37% macro F1 and absence of prospective policy tests constrain behavioral claims.
items.attribution: Li et al. — arXiv preprint (survey-grounded economic multi-agent framework)

items.streamTitle: Relationally persuasive AI increased both helpful reliance and harmful overreliance
items.streamSummary: A randomized 462-adult study found relational AI framing increased reliance on both correct and incorrect advice. Accuracy sensitivity and the proposed trust mechanism remain unproven.
items.attribution: Mizrak, Kirgiz and Demirel — Journal of Intelligence (randomized experiment)

items.streamTitle: Self-evolving agent evaluations caught regressions hidden by final benchmark scores
items.streamSummary: SEAGym separated agent-harness validation, held-out transfer and replay. An intermediate snapshot collapsed to 6/80 solved tasks, revealing a regression that final scores hid.
items.attribution: Zheng et al. — arXiv preprint (SEAGym agent evaluation)

items.streamTitle: Higher-order opinion model represented group interactions beyond pairwise social ties
items.streamSummary: An IEEE model replaces purely pairwise opinion links with group-level hypergraph interactions and derives convergence properties. Its simulated dynamics are not validated human intervention forecasts.
items.attribution: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems — formal opinion-dynamics study

items.streamTitle: Transferred pedestrian models preserved network hierarchy after local calibration
items.streamSummary: A November 2 mobility study transferred behavior models between cities and found persistent network hierarchy after observed-count calibration. Fitted agreement is not an independent prospective test.
items.attribution: Nourmohammadi, Rashidi and Saberi — npj Sustainable Mobility and Transport (transfer/calibration study)
